correctness.rationale: Ottaviani--Sodomaco--Ventura reproduce the GKZ exponential generating function \(\sum H_dx^d/d!=e^{-2x}(1-x)^{-2}\) and the coefficient formula \(H_d=d!A_d\) with \(A_d=\sum_{j=0}^d(d-j+1)(-2)^j/j!\), and record \(\operatorname{EDdegree}_F((\mathbb P^1)^d)=d!\). Legendre gives \(\nu_2(2^j/j!)=s_2(j)\). For even d, the j=0 term of \(A_d\) is odd and all others are even, so \(A_d\) is odd. For odd d, every j>=2 term is divisible by 4 in the 2-adic integers: even j adds an even factor \(d-j+1\), while odd j>=3 has \(s_2(j)\ge2\). Thus \(A_d\equiv(d+1)-2d=1-d\pmod4\), giving exact valuation one for \(d\equiv3\pmod4\) and valuation at least two for \(d\equiv1\pmod4\). The inspected exact checker independently reconstructs the recurrence and coefficient formula and verifies the phase law through d=4000; this is regression evidence only.
correctness.risk: The \(d\equiv1\pmod4\) branch intentionally gives only a lower bound on the additional valuation.

The OEIS record A087981 lists the same sequence, recurrence, formula and a general permanent divisibility lower bound, but it does not state the residue-sensitive exact valuation law. The modern full-text Segre-degree paper likewise gives the exact degree and ED-degree formulas without the dyadic classification. Resultary searches returned the audited phase law as the direct match and no earlier dominating p-adic theorem.

value.rationale: The degree is a canonical invariant of the binary Segre dual hypersurface, and its exact two-primary behavior is a natural arithmetic invariant. The theorem identifies a clean residue phase and relates it to the equally natural Frobenius ED degree via Legendre's formula. It is an exact infinite statement rather than a table recomputation, and the \(d\equiv1\pmod4\) variability is stated honestly.
value.risk: The proof is short once the classical coefficient formula is known, so the contribution is a focused arithmetic invariant rather than a broad geometric theorem.

final_claim: For the degree \(H_d\) of the \(2^{\times d}\) hyperdeterminant, \(\nu_2(H_d)=d-s_2(d)\) for even \(d\), equals \(d-s_2(d)+1\) for \(d\equiv3\pmod4\), and is at least \(d-s_2(d)+2\) for \(d\equiv1\pmod4\); since the Frobenius ED degree of \((\mathbb P^1)^d\) is \(d!\), these are the exact first dyadic excess layers over \(\nu_2(d!)\).
limitations: No exact formula for the excess valuation is claimed when \(d\equiv1\pmod4\).
